target_customer: Colleges and universities (registrars, provosts, academic operations offices)
problem: Universities build course schedules, curricula and catalogs in clumsy legacy systems and spreadsheets. Coursedog layers modern scheduling, curriculum and catalog software over the student information system.
business_model: B2B SaaS annual contracts per institution

founders.name: Justin Wenig
education: Columbia University (student when the company started, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: Dormmate of Diao at Columbia per TechCrunch 2020.

founders.name: Nicholas Diao
education: Columbia University (student when the company started, per TechCrunch)
previous_startups: Omega Strategies (founder and CEO per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CTO.

competitors.name: Blackboard and legacy student information systems
competitors.what: Incumbent university software that Coursedog sits on top of rather than replacing
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch in March 2020 as one of the two big software tools in universities

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling plus integrations with student information systems like Banner and PeopleSoft are standard engineering with some hard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated into the registrar workflow and SIS, universities rarely switch, but entrants can copy features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying it; Coursedog raised growth capital in 2021 and 2023 and bought ClassRanked in April 2026.

market_need_then: Founders felt the pain as students struggling to register for a popular class at Columbia in 2018. By 2020 more than 60 institutions were customers, starting with Columbia Law School.

branding.domain_note: Uses coursedog.com, an exact match; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Logo exists, design not described in sources opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, friendly, partner-like; tagline Higher Ed's Best Friend

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name and a friendly tagline in a niche vertical; no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Coursedog grew from a Columbia dorm idea into a vendor with roughly 100 institutions by 2021 and a reported 500 plus campuses later, funded by a 2020 seed, a 2021 Coatue Series A and a 2023 JMI growth investment. The YC directory labels it Acquired, yet sources found describe JMI as a growth investor and Coursedog itself as an acquirer of ClassRanked in 2026, so the Acquired label may reflect a stale or loose tag. Success came from a painful, sticky workflow sold to institutions through an SIS integration.
notes: YC status says Acquired but no acquisition of Coursedog was found; exit type set to unknown. YC long description cites 100m from JMI while the Business Wire and law firm headline says 90M; 90M used. Businesswire page returned 403. Ad Astra and CollegeNET are positioned as rivals on Coursedog's own comparison pages but those are undated, so not listed as competitors at founding.
